Donor pseudobulk counts for each cell type

Source: R/pseudobulk.R
donor_pseudobulk.Rd

Sums the raw counts of each cell type within each donor and returns one SummarizedExperiment per cell type, with the donors' exposure data as column data. These are the pseudobulk counts that run_sc_exwas and the other pseudobulk functions of the package aggregate internally, so they can be passed to other Bioconductor tools, inspected, or plotted.

Usage

donor_pseudobulk(
  x,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  celltypes = NULL,
  min_cells = 10L
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment with a "counts" assay. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

celltype_col

Character. Column in colData containing cell type annotations. Default "cell_type".

celltypes

Character vector (optional). Cell types to aggregate. Default: all non-missing labels, sorted.

min_cells

Integer. A donor is included for a cell type only when it has at least this many cells of that type. Default 10, the default of run_sc_exwas.

Value

A SimpleList named by cell type. Each element is a SummarizedExperiment with one column per included donor and

  • an assay "counts" with the summed raw counts (features by donors);

  • rowData copied from x;

  • colData with the donor identifier (donor_id), the cell type (cell_type), the number of cells summed (n_cells) and one column per variable of exposureData(x);

  • metadata recording the cell type, min_cells and the colData columns used for donors and cell types.

Cell types in which no donor reaches min_cells are left out and listed in metadata(result)$skipped.

Details

The summation is done by scrapper::aggregateAcrossCells(). Donors with missing exposure values are kept here; the analysis functions drop them, and filter genes, when they fit a model, so a fitted model may use fewer donors and genes than the object returned here. Model diagnostics (metadata() of the run_sc_exwas result) list the donors and gene counts actually used.

References

Lun ATL, Kancherla J (2023). Powering single-cell analyses in the browser with WebAssembly. Journal of Open Source Software 8(89):5603. doi:10.21105/joss.05603

See also

run_sc_exwas

Examples

library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rpois(2000, 5), nrow = 20,
    dimnames = list(paste0("G", 1:20), paste0("c", 1:100)))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = DataFrame(donor_id = rep(paste0("D", 1:5), each = 20),
        cell_type = rep(c("Mono", "NK"), 50)))
exp_mat <- matrix(rnorm(5), ncol = 1,
    dimnames = list(paste0("D", 1:5), "E1"))
scee <- build_scee(sce, exp_mat, sample_col = "donor_id")
pb <- donor_pseudobulk(scee, min_cells = 5L)
pb
#> List of length 2
#> names(2): Mono NK
SummarizedExperiment::colData(pb[["Mono"]])
#> DataFrame with 5 rows and 4 columns
#>       donor_id   cell_type   n_cells         E1
#>    <character> <character> <integer>  <numeric>
#> D1          D1        Mono        10  1.1349651
#> D2          D2        Mono        10  1.1119318
#> D3          D3        Mono        10 -0.8707776
#> D4          D4        Mono        10  0.2107316
#> D5          D5        Mono        10  0.0693956
